metadata.title: Tesla Just Made the Cybertruck $5,000 More Expensive

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Tesla Inc. (TSLA, Financials) just made the Cybertruck pricier for U.S. buyers. The business said on its website that it raised pricing Tuesday for two models of the electric pickup by $5,000.The dual-motor Cybertruck now starts at $74,990, with the premium all-wheel-drive model beginning at $84,990.These hikes are important since Tesla has often used pricing as a lever to manage demand, profitability and production across its array of vehicles. That makes the current move interesting for the Cybertruck.The truck has been one of the most keenly anticipated launches for Tesla, in part because of its unorthodox appearance, and in part because investors have been waiting to see if it can become a big contributor alongside the Model 3 and Model Y.If demand holds up, a higher sticker price could help margins, but it also raises the cost of entry for purchasers when consumers have lots of electric and regular pickup choices.The Reuters report did not give a reason for the hike from Tesla. This is the bigger concern now, whether consumers accept the extra $5,000 with a major impact to Cybertruck demand.
